newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian police fire shots at anti-Burma protest.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian police fire shots at anti-Burma protest.

text.p: Police fired shots in the air near the U.S. Embassy as opposition leader Sam Rainsy led a march through the Cambodian capital on Wednesday to protest against the visit of Burmese leader General Than Shwe.

An hour after the protest, Than Shwe arrived in Phnom Penh at the head of a 44-member entourage and was greeted by King Norodom Sihanouk and co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen at the airport.

In what Sam Rainsy called a game of urban guerrilla warfare, hundreds of police pursued several dozen protesters through the streets, hastily setting up road blocks in a vain attempt to thwart the hour-long demonstration in support of Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi.
Sam Rainsy, who met Suu Kyi in Rangoon in August, heads the Khmer Nation Party, which is not recognised by the Phnom Penh government.

Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) recently barred opposition leader Syu Kyi from giving regular weekly speeches at her home and has blocked access to her residence since Saturday.
Late last month, the SLORC arrested hundreds of Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party activists and released them in stages.

No one was seriously injured in Wednesday's protest, but witnesses said one of the demonstrators was beaten and reporters were manhandled. A police official said two policemen were injured when a protester's car struck them at a barricade.
Sam Rainsy said in a statement that his driver and a bodyguard were arrested. He told reporters that one of the men was beaten and the front lights of the car he drove were smashed.

But Mok Chito, director of the penal police, said only the driver had been arrested. He said the driver had run over two government soldiers, breaking the leg of one and slightly injuring another in the arm.
"It was like cat and mouse, like urban guerrilla warfare," Sam Rainsy said.
As the demonstrators approached the U.S. Embassy to speak with Ambassador Kenneth Quinn, one policeman near the rear of the crowd released a burst of gunfire in the air to try to halt them.
A second policeman, looking panicked as protesters pushed past him, fired a second burst in front of the embassy.
As demonstrators waved signs saying "Aung San Suu Kyi is a model for Asia" and "Long live the NLD," Sam Rainsy entered the embassy and briefly spoke to the ambassador, witnesses said.
He said Quinn had told him U.S. officials would not greet Than Shwe at the airport.
Ambassadors from three European countries -- Germany, France and Britain -- were introduced to Than Shwe on his arrival at the airport.
One of the diplomats said: "We are not too keen on this."
